newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas Methodist Hosp revs rated BBB - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas Methodist Hosp revs rated BBB - S&P.

text.p: NEW YORK, Sept 25 - Standard & Poor's Corp today said it has assigned its triple-B' rating to Paragould, Ark.'s $15 million hospital revenue bonds series 1996, issued for Arkansas Methodist Hospital.

The rating reflects a strong financial profile characterized by consistently excellent earnings, healthy cash flow, and growing liquidity. Factors precluding a higher rating include aggressive capital plans, concentrated medical staff, and a restrictive payor mix.

Strict cost controls, revenue enhancements, light managed care, and volume growth produce strong earnings. Admissions at the 129-bed hospital increased 6.4% over the past three years to 4,117 patients in fiscal 1996. Outpatient visits also grew 6% over the same period. Operating and excess margins averaged 8% and 10%, respectively, from fiscal 1992-1996. The strong earnings and manageable pro forma debt burden produced maximum debt service coverage above 2.40 times over the past three years. Because of the excellent profits, aggressive accounts receivable collection, and moderate capital expenses, cash and investments increased to $15.4 million, or 265 days' operating expenses in fiscal 1996, from $6.2 million or 129 days' three year earlier.

However, the hospital is embarking on a substantial $20 million modernization and expansion project, mostly to accommodate ambulatory services. The project's major components include outpatient surgery, medical office, women's unit, and physical therapy additions, along with emergency room, surgery, and imaging department renovations. A $5 million equity contribution will finance the 17-physician medical office building. Nonetheless, post-issuance cash compares favorably to debt and remains healthy at $10.4 million, or 183 days operating expenses. A healthy $24.8 million equity position comfortably supports the new debt, evidenced by 38% pro forma debt to capitalization.

Successful physician recruitment and service additions increased primary service area inpatient market share to 50% in fiscal 1996, from historical 46% levels. Direct competition in the hospital's northeastern Arkansas service area is limited, but out-migration to Jonesboro, 22 miles south, remains high. Management anticipates that the master facilities plan will continue boosting its physician recruitment success and reduce its reliance on the top-10 revenue producing doctors, which currently generate 62% of total revenue. Moreover, while the medical staff has grown to 28 active admitters, the hospital remains vulnerable because of its small size. Although Medicare accounts for a high 55.6% of revenue, the hospital's favorable cost structure allows it to generate a profit under the program.
The outlook anticipates project completion on time and within budget. It also expects consistent profitability and cash flow generation, not necessarily at historical levels, Standard & Poor's said.
